rationale: Chapter 10 explains how to read regime evidence over time and why the Weekly Score should remain descriptive context rather than a forecast or trading signal.

Chapter 10 supplies the book's regime-history context for interpreting the Score's construction, recalculation limits and descriptive validation without turning historical alignment into predictive evidence.
Chapter 11 supplies the driver-first weekly sequence behind this report: identify the dominant driver, then check dollar direction, real rates, liquidity stress and asset-specific evidence.
Chapter 4 explains how to separate the active transmission channel when liquidity support, oil-linked inflation pressure and rates are pulling in different directions.
Chapter 5 explains why EIA inventories, refinery activity and the physical oil balance must be checked before treating an oil move as a dollar-only trade.
